key_insight: A first-principles nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter plus ab initio molecular dynamics framework separates electronic and lattice effects in CH3NH3PbBr3 transient absorption, showing electrons dominate at femtoseconds while thermal lattice effects emerge at picoseconds.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mechanistic basis for interpreting pump-probe spectra in perovskite solar cells and for targeting ultrafast optoelectronic responses via electronic screening and lattice dynamics.
method: Nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter equation to model transient excitonic response
Ab initio molecular dynamics to capture thermal lattice motion
Time-resolved decomposition of electronic vs lattice contributions across fs-to-ps scales
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative agreement in disentangling transient absorption across femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales, with distinct spectral mechanisms identified for X-ray and optical probes.
watch_item: The approach is computationally intensive and material-specific, so transferability to larger device-scale systems or strongly disordered samples may be limited.
paper_title: Disentangling Electronic and Lattice Contributions to Transient Absorption in Metal Halide Perovskites: A First-Principles Study of CH3NH3PbBr3
